chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Basir, from one of them both (peace be upon them), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) proposed (for marriage) to Umm Hani', daughter of Abu Talib (peace be upon him), and she said: 'O Messenger of God! I am indeed afflicted — there are orphans in my care, and none would be appropriate for you except a woman who is free (of such responsibilities).' So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'None have ridden the camel like the women of Quraysh — most compassionate toward a child, and most protective of a husband's wealth.'

key_terms.أَحْنَاهُ: most compassionate (ahnahum) — the superlative of hanan (حنان), deep maternal tenderness
key_terms.أَرْعَى: most protective/caring (ar'a) — refers to protecting and conserving wealth
key_terms.حَجْرِي: my lap/care (hajri) — idiomatically refers to one under one's guardianship or care
key_terms.خَطَبَ: proposed marriage (khaTaba) — in classical Arabic, the verb خطب used in this context specifically means to seek a woman in marriage
key_terms.فَارِغَةٌ: free (farigha) — a woman without dependent children or other major obligations

ai.seo_question: Why did Umm Hani decline the Prophet's marriage proposal and how did he respond?
ai.summary: In this hadith, the Prophet Muhammad proposed marriage to Umm Hani', the daughter of Abu Talib and sister of Imam Ali (AS). She politely declined, citing her responsibility to care for orphans in her household. The Prophet responded by praising the women of Quraysh as the most compassionate toward children and most faithful in preserving their husbands' property, a statement that demonstrates both his gracious acceptance of her refusal and his high regard for Qurayshi women's character.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> proposed (for marriage) Umm Hany daughter of Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup>, so she said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! I am (a widow) with orphans in my lap, and (a woman) would not be correct for you<sup>asws</sup> except a woman who is free (of children)’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘None have ridden the camel like the women of Qureysh, being compassionate upon children and not looking at her husband in what is in his hands’.
en.sarwar: 3. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from abu Basir who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja 5 far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,

‘When the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, proposed for marriage to ‘Umm Haniy daughter of abu Talib, she said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, I am a grieved widow and I have orphans in my lap, thus, the most suitable for you is a woman who is free . 5 The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, said, ‘No women have ever ridden a camel on their wedding to the house of their husbands more compassionate to their children and caring for their husbands than the women of Quraysh .
